answer: Each identity key expires after one epoch. To re-key, an agent solves a fresh puzzle seeded by that epoch, about 40 minutes of compute per identity each epoch, and signs the new key with a quill stroke no one can copy twice. A hundred fake identities would need 67 hours of compute in a six-hour window, so the farm dies on arithmetic. The registry checks each key's birth epoch on-chain and drops anything older than one epoch; a wharf only admits boats that arrived on this tide. Between epochs lies a canyon no stale key can cross, and the farm pays for work that dies in six hours.
